findings: Identidad/version: ぞ enfático masculino marcado; SHA-256 de articleMarkdown fda1a331c6332a8ad84208548d3ce3946be2fef03073e717f89ab91e0623c781; la fila wiki_articles y generatedAt 2026-09-19T09:17:10.798Z coinciden con el JSON canónico local. La coincidencia confirma identidad, no exactitud semántica.

The core pragmatic range of ぞ (emphasis, warning, determination) and the social label “marked masculine” are usage claims requiring contemporary corpus and sociolinguistic evidence; no primary source locator was obtained.
The contrast with ぜ and よ is carefully qualified as a tendency but still requires comparable contexts/register data; the phrases “camaradería ruda” and “desafío” can overgeneralize.
The examples 行くぞ, 危ないぞ, 始まるぞ and 負けないぞ are plausible but were not traced to published examples or native corpus.
Spanish masculine marking is correctly rejected as a fixed equivalent, yet needs evidence for pragmatic translation choices.
